{{Short description|Theorem of real analysis}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Zahorski's theorem''' is a theorem of [[real analysis]]. It states that a necessary and sufficient condition for a subset of the [[real line]] to be the set of points of non-differentiability of a continuous real-valued function, is that it be the union of a [[G-delta set|G<sub>&delta;</sub> set]] and a <math>{G_\delta}_\sigma</math> set of [[zero measure]].

This result was proved by {{Interlanguage link multi|Zygmunt Zahorski|pl}} in 1939 and first published in 1941.
